PMU301H1.description: An introduction into the history and functionality of the piano. This course touches on nomenclature for the instrument, how the action works, and how better understanding the structure and mechanics of the instrument can enhance the playing of a pianist.

PMU401H1.name: The Business of Music
PMU401H1.title: The Business of Music
PMU401H1.description: A study of the strategies and tools used by music industry professionals to define their creative identity, obtain paid work, market themselves, and operate within professional social spaces. Students develop public-relations materials that are ready for professional use and interact with prominent industry insiders.

SMU200H1.name: Healthy Prac-Healthy Musicians
SMU200H1.title: Healthy Practices for Healthy Musicians
SMU200H1.description: This course introduces students to the field of musicians' health through a blend of physical practices and theoretical discussions. Each class includes a yoga-based movement practice and a discussions of relevant concepts including basic anatomy for musicians, motor learning techniques, and strategies for addressing performance anxiety and achieving peak performance. Students will leave the course with a repertoire of stretches and exercises to counterbalance strains associated with playing their instruments, strategies to make effective use of practice time, and an awareness of available health resources in the community and online.

SMU400H1.name: Intro to Music Health
SMU400H1.title: Introduction to Music in Healthcare
SMU400H1.description: This course explores culturally responsive music-based interventions in healthcare contexts including music therapy, music and medicine, community music and artists working in interdisciplinary teams. Through a universal-design framework, students examine critical issues, current research and data driven practice, developing skills to design music and health initiatives.

TMU130H1.name: Music Theory I
TMU130H1.title: Music Theory I
TMU130H1.description: Diatonic harmony. Principles of voice leading and harmonic progression. Introduction to musical form.

TMU132H1.name: Musical Skills I
TMU132H1.title: Musical Skills I
TMU132H1.description: Reading and listening skills for diatonic materials. Topics include sight singing, rhythm reading, keyboard harmony, and dictation.

TMU230H1.name: Music Theory III
TMU230H1.title: Music Theory III
TMU230H1.description: Form & Analysis. Study of forms and analysis of repertoire from c. 1700-c. 1900. Forms to be studied include binary, ternary, sonata, rondo, variation, and fugue.

TMU316H1.name: Counterpoint I
TMU316H1.title: Counterpoint I
TMU316H1.description: Practical and analytical study of 18th-century contrapuntal techniques, including species writing, canon and invention. Two hours.

TMU499H1.name: Independent Study
TMU499H1.title: Independent Study
TMU499H1.description: An intensive research project under the supervision of a faculty member. The project must be academically/artistically demanding and uniquely suitable for the individual student. Students propose a topic that is currently not covered in the curriculum or one that warrants further exploration related to research interests and/or musical goals. Available to 4th year students with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.3(B+) and availability of a full-time faculty advisor from the Theory & Composition division. Modes of assessment are determined through discussion between student and supervisor, but will usually include a public presentation of the research project.

TMU499Y1.name: [No course title available]
TMU499Y1.title: Independent Study
TMU499Y1.description: Available to students in 4th year who have maintained first-class standing in their first three years of study.

EMU268H1.name: Instrumental: Bassoon
EMU268H1.title: Instrumental Class: Bassoon
EMU268H1.description: Introductory study of the bassoon. One hour, one term.

HMU319H1.name: Music, Gender and Sexuality
HMU319H1.title: Music, Gender and Sexuality
HMU319H1.description: An inquiry into the construction and reflection of gender and sexual identities in Western music. The course will emphasize discourses surrounding feminism and the role of women in music, masculinity studies, and gay, lesbian, bi-sexual and transgendered studies and their relationships to musical specific works, production and reception.

HMU386H1.name: Social Lives of Mus Instrument
HMU386H1.title: Social Lives of Musical Instruments
HMU386H1.description: This course examines how musical instruments shape sounds and meanings in various sociocultural and historical contexts. Examples including but not limited to indigenous drums on Turtle Island, violins in the Middle East, and electric guitars in North America illustrate instruments' entanglements with issues such as gender, genre, national identity, etc.

HMU385H1.name: Intro to Sound Studies
HMU385H1.title: Introduction to Sound Studies
HMU385H1.description: This course introduces students to the interdisciplinary field of sound studies by exploring how people perceive and engage with everyday sounds, especially in urban settings. Topics may include, but are not limited to noise, silence, acoustic communities, soundscapes, media, and various sound technologies.

JMU302H1.name: Advanced Ear Training & Harmony
JMU302H1.title: Advanced Ear Training & Harmony
JMU302H1.description: A continuation of JMU201Y1, this course addresses advanced ear training and theoretical concepts including "upper structure" voicings/chord extentions which are commonly found in post-bebop and contemporary jazz harmony. Analysis and performance of the work of influential composers such as Wayne Shorter and Kenny Wheeler will be central in this course.

JMU420H1.name: Adv Jazz Arranging & Orch I
JMU420H1.title: Advanced Jazz Arranging & Orchestration I
JMU420H1.description: To develop the skills necessary to produce arrangements for large ensembles. These principles of arranging will be applied to various combinations of instruments including but not limited to 5 saxophones, 5 trumpets, 4 trombones, guitar, piano, bass, drums, and voice.

PMU262H1.name: Piano Teaching Methods Practicum
PMU262H1.title: Piano Teaching Methods Practicum
PMU262H1.description: Practical experiences in teaching beginner to intermediate level adult pianists and observations of children’s private lessons and group classes in the University of Toronto Piano Pedagogy Program.

PMU452Y1.name: Piano-Vocal Masterclass
PMU452Y1.title: Piano-Vocal Master Class
PMU452Y1.description: An exploration of the standard vocal literature. Pianists prepare and perform with student singers. One hour.

PMU455Y1.name: Piano-Vocal Masterclass
PMU455Y1.title: Piano-Vocal Master Class
PMU455Y1.description: Students prepare and perform vocal music with the pianists in PMU352Y1.
PMU455Y1.prereqText: Voice performance majors or P.I., In Year 4.

TMU307H1.name: Analysis I
TMU307H1.title: Music Analysis I: Methods and Repertoires, 1750-1840
TMU307H1.description: In-depth analysis of musical works from c. 1750 to 1840; study of recent analytical approaches to music and meaning, musical form, and text-music relationships; selected readings. TMU307H1 can be taken before, after, or independently from TMU308H1.

TMU404H1.name: Extended Tonal Tech. in 20th Century Music
TMU404H1.title: Extended Tonal Techniques in 20th Century Music
TMU404H1.description: An analytical study of the music of Debussy, Bartok, Stravinsky and others. The course will focus on harmony (modes, scales, chords), rhythm, form, and methods of motivic and thematic development.

DMU409H1.name: Songwriting
DMU409H1.title: Songwriting
DMU409H1.description: For nearly a century, songwriting has been foremost a recording art. Today’s songwriter must have a firm command of music production techniques to faithfully express their songwriting vision. This course examines essential and advanced production techniques used by chart-topping pop songs. Hidden structures and psychoacoustics, narratives and emotional impact, are recurring themes. Considerations for composing contemporary vocal melodies, the narrative implications of harmonic choices, a compelling verse and chorus design, and effective lyrical writing are all dissected. Basic experience with a DAW is recommended; students produce songs within their DAW of choice. The course culminates in a songwriting showcase.
DMU409H1.prereqText: TMU231H1 or JMU200Y1 (Faculty of Music); DMU111H1, TMU131H1 (Faculty of Arts & Science)

TMU400H1.name: Feminist Listening: Intersectional App: N.American Popular Music
TMU400H1.title: Feminist Listening: Intersectional Approaches to North American Popular Music
TMU400H1.description: This course develops modes of feminist listening to North American popular music. Drawing on intersectional analytical tools, it examines a wide repertory of music, including pop, rock, R&B, hip-hop, jazz, blues, country, and indie, and develops students’ abilities to hear and discuss music in relation to gender/sexuality/race/ethnicity/ability/power.

CMU113H1.name: Introduction to Composition II
CMU113H1.title: Introduction to Composition II
CMU113H1.description: An extension of the material taught in TMU112H1.

DMU412H1.name: Interactive Music & Sound - Video Games II
DMU412H1.title: Interactive Music and Sound for Video Games II
DMU412H1.description: Students expand on their knowledge of game audio implementation by using RTPCs to create real-time dynamic and modular sound design and music systems using middleware software such as FMOD and Wwise. Students work on a cross-discipline video game development project in collaboration with students specializing in computer science and animation/design.

EMU135H1.name: Intro to Community Music Engagement
EMU135H1.title: Introduction to Community Music Engagement
EMU135H1.description: This course introduces students to a variety of ways in which music and musicking are embedded in local communities. Students will critically reflect on current practices and research by leaders in community music engagement. Themes of anti-oppression, belonging, wholeness, and wellbeing will be central to the course.

EMU154H1.name: Inst Class: Guitar
EMU154H1.title: Instrumental Class: Guitar
EMU154H1.description: Introductory study of the guitar. Pedagogical considerations for class guitar instruction in popular and classical guitar styles.

EMU231H1.name: Voice Pedagogy for Young Choir
EMU231H1.title: Voice Pedagogy for Young Choirs
EMU231H1.description: Introductory study of vocal methods for teaching young choirs with attention to breathing techniques, tone production, vocal diction and rehearsal pedagogies relevant to working with children and youth choirs. Recommended for all students interested in learning to work vocally with young singers, ages 6-16.

EMU240H1.name: Theoretical Inquiry in Mus Ed
EMU240H1.title: Theoretical Inquiry in Music Education
EMU240H1.description: This course introduces students to theoretical inquiry in music education in the context of diversity related to students, teachers, music, and music educational settings. Through course readings, individual research, classroom interactions, presentations, and writing short essays, students critique existing theories, and develop concepts articulating their own theories of music education that take into account relevant social, political, and ethical questions.

EMU270H1.name: Instrumental: Double Bass
EMU270H1.title: Instrumental Class: Double Bass
EMU270H1.description: Introductory study of the double bass. One hour, one term.

EMU360H1.name: Jazz Improvisation
EMU360H1.title: Jazz Improvisation for Music Education
EMU360H1.description: Development of improvisation skills through applied performance and theoretical analysis in a variety of jazz styles.

EMU371H1.name: Multimodal Approach-Mus Training
EMU371H1.title: Multimodal Approaches to Music Teaching and Learning
EMU371H1.description: This course provides a multitude of approaches to music teaching and learning including informal music learning, music technology, community music and improvisatory and creative musical activities in music classrooms. Students will actively create and perform music while crafting a well-rounded curriculum based on the ideas derived from the course. Philosophical underpinnings of such practices will also be examined.

EMU401H1.name: Calls to Action through Mus Ed
EMU401H1.title: Calls to Action through Music Education
EMU401H1.description: This course takes the Calls to Action from the Truth and Reconciliation Commission as the Foundation for Curriculum and Pedagogy in Music Education. Students will lead seminars on topics related to their research interest and examine current issues facing Indigenous Peoples through the lens of Reconciliation.

EMU431H1.name: Choral Lit & Conducting II
EMU431H1.title: Choral Literature & Conducting II
EMU431H1.description: The study of choral literature and conducting technique with an emphasis on European classical and Contemporary choral music (including selected choral-orchestral repertoire). The weekly class will meet in a combined literature and seminar and conducting practicum with piano and/or small instrumental ensemble.

EMU485H1.name: Advanced Topics in Music & Childhood
EMU485H1.title: Advanced Topics in Music and Childhood
EMU485H1.description: This course invites students to expand their strategies for welcoming children into the diverse practice of musicking. At the core is bell hook’s philosophy of education as a practice of freedom as well as culturally responsive, culturally relevant, and culturally sustaining approaches to music education.

EMU499Y1.name: [No course title available]
EMU499Y1.title: Independent Study
EMU499Y1.description: Available to students in 3rd or 4th year on successful completion of several EMU courses, depending on grade standing and availability of instructor.

HMU126H1.name: Historical Survey II
HMU126H1.title: Historical Survey II
HMU126H1.description: Western music from 1750 to the present.
HMU126H1.exclusionText: HMU226H1. Does not count as an HMU elective.

HMU340H1.name: Music in North America
HMU340H1.title: Music in North America
HMU340H1.description: Study of music in North American life. Topics may include folk and popular music, jazz and art music.

HMU345H1.name: Global Popular Musics
HMU345H1.title: Global Popular Musics
HMU345H1.description: Global Popular Musics is an introduction to popular music in its social and cultural context in a variety of international settings. Genres to be covered may include, but are not limited to, rock, hip-hop, country, and “world music”. The course will take an issues-based approach to the study of popular music, focusing on topics such as the interplay of tradition and modernity; media and technology; race, gender, sexuality, class, and other facets of identity; urbanization and migration; and the markets and legal structures surrounding music.

HMU435H1.name: Topics in Ethnomusic:Current I ssues
HMU435H1.title: Topics in Ethnomusicology: Current Issues
HMU435H1.description: An undergraduate seminar devoted to exploring an emergent sub-field of ethnomusicology. The sub-field to be explored will rotate, but some examples are: the study of music and gender, race, or class; music and language; music and violence; sociomusicology; medical ethnomusicology; the ethnomusicology of popular music and technology; analytical approaches in ethnomusicology.
HMU435H1.prereqText: Completion of 4-course History and Culture requirement.

JMU215H1.name: Jazz History II
JMU215H1.title: Jazz History II
JMU215H1.description: Jazz History II begins in the 1960s with the music that ushered in the modern era of jazz (Miles Davis Quintet, free/avant-garde, jazz-rock). It explores the myriad paths and styles that have been incorporated by jazz musicians of the past fifty years, up to the present day.

JMU303H1.name: Rhythm for Improvisers
JMU303H1.title: Rhythm for Improvisers
JMU303H1.description: This course focuses on methods for students to expand their rhythmic vocabulary as improvisers and composers. Motivis development, rhythmic modulation and odd time signature playing will be addressed. Analysis and performance of the music of influential contemporary composers such as Dave Holland will be central to this course.

JMU305H1.name: Introduction to Jazz Theory
JMU305H1.title: Introduction to Jazz Theory
JMU305H1.description: An introduction to jazz theory for music students not in a jazz program. Course includes analysis and written exercises in various jazz forms and idioms. Some listening and improvisation activities may be included to reinforce and apply theoretical concepts.

MMU100H1.name: Lives in Music
MMU100H1.title: Lives in Music
MMU100H1.description: A survey of career paths that begin with an undergraduate degree in music. Discussion of the competencies required in various musical professions and strategies to develop them during undergraduate study. Classes led by members of the Faculty of Music teaching staff and guest lecturers.

MMU201H1.name: Creative Identities Music II
MMU201H1.title: Creative Identities in Music II
MMU201H1.description: This course is a continuation of MMU200, designed to help students develop a personalized roadmap for future professional work. Assignments include creating a digital "Mini-festo," team debates, group role-playing exercises, video journals, analytical writing, and a major project.

MMU400H1.name: Starting a Music Enterprise
MMU400H1.title: Starting a Music Enterprise
MMU400H1.description: This course focuses on developing potential business or project opportunities that are centered on music. The course provides tools to move from opportunity identification to idea generation and the launch of a music enterprise. Students develop an assessment process to determine the desirability, feasibility, and sustainability of a new enterprise.

PMA452Y1.name: Piano-vocal Mast Cla
PMA452Y1.title: Piano-Vocal Master Class
PMA452Y1.description: An exploration of the standard vocal literature. Pianists prepare and perform with student singers. One hour.

PMA455Y1.name: Piano-vocal Mast Cl
PMA455Y1.title: Piano-Vocal Master Class
PMA455Y1.description: Students prepare and perform vocal music with the pianists in PMA452Y. P.I.

PMU129H1.name: Italian Vocal Repertoire
PMU129H1.title: Italian Vocal Repertoire
PMU129H1.description: Practical study through in-class coaching on authentic pronunciation and interpretation. Emphasis on the art song repertoire of the seventeenth to twentieth centuries.

PMU229H1.name: Italian Vocal Repertoire
PMU229H1.title: Italian Vocal Repertoire
PMU229H1.description: A continuation of PMU129H1. Practical study through in-class coaching on authentic pronunciation and interpretation. Emphasis on the art song repertoire of the seventeenth to twentieth centuries.
PMU229H1.prereqText: PMU129H1 - Voice Performance majors or P.I.

PMU352Y1.name: Piano-Vocal Masterclass
PMU352Y1.title: Piano-Vocal Master Class
PMU352Y1.description: An exploration of the standard vocal literature. Pianists prepare and perform with student singers. One hour.

PMU355Y1.name: Piano-Vocal Masterclass
PMU355Y1.title: Piano-Vocal Master Class
PMU355Y1.description: Students prepare and perform vocal music with the pianists in PMU352Y1.
PMU355Y1.prereqText: Voice Performance majors or P.I., In Year 3.

PMU408H1.name: Performing as a Freelance Artist in North America
PMU408H1.title: Performing as a Freelance Artist in North America
PMU408H1.description: This course prepares students for a freelance career in North America—including a detailed study of current industry showcases, financing of productions, advanced negotiation, technical production (from the artist’s perspective), self-advocacy, and US work visas. Students will understand the artistic demands, finances, lifestyle, and carbon impact of a freelance touring career.

SMU402H1.name: Introduction to Music Therapy
SMU402H1.title: Introduction to Music Therapy
SMU402H1.description: This course offers a survey of music therapy practices in Canada and across the world, and gives students a broad overview of different clinical populations, aims and objectives, clinical care settings, history and philosophies of music therapy, and practice styles, including bio-medical, psychotherapeutic, and rehabilitative approaches. Case studies and relevant research are to be examined and explored.

SMU499H1.name: Independent Study
SMU499H1.title: Independent Study
SMU499H1.description: Available to students in 4th year on successful completion of their third year with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.3 (B+) and availability of a full-time faculty advisor from the Music & Health subdivision. Students propose a topic that is currently not covered in the curriculum or one that warrants further exploration related to research interests and/or musical goals. Modes of assessment are determined through discussion between student and supervisor, but will usually include a public presentation of the research project.

TMU131H1.name: Music Theory II
TMU131H1.title: Music Theory II
TMU131H1.description: Chromatic harmony. Topics include modulation, mixture, Neapolitan and augmented sixths.

TMU133H1.name: Musical Skills II
TMU133H1.title: Musical Skills II
TMU133H1.description: Reading and listening skills for chromatic materials. Topics include sight singing, rhythm reading, keyboard harmony, and dictation.

TMU231H1.name: Music Theory IV
TMU231H1.title: Music Theory IV
TMU231H1.description: Post-tonal theory and analysis. Study of compositional practices in music written after 1900.

TMU232H1.name: Musical Skills III
TMU232H1.title: Musical Skills III
TMU232H1.description: Advanced reading and listening skills suitable for understanding post-tonal music. Topics include modes, sets, and innovations in rhythm and meter, practiced through exercises in sight singing, rhythm, dictation, keyboard, and aural analysis.

TMU317H1.name: Counterpoint II
TMU317H1.title: Counterpoint II
TMU317H1.description: Continuation of TMU316H1 including chorale prelude and fugue. Two hours.

HMU125H1.name: Survey of Western Music History I
HMU125H1.title: Survey of Western Music History I
HMU125H1.description: This course surveys genres and repertoires of Western music in historical contexts between c1600-1825, while developing students’ techniques and skills in researching and writing effectively about music.

CMU420H1.name: Composing for Percussion
CMU420H1.title: Composing for Percussion
CMU420H1.description: The course will examine in detail the use of percussion in contemporary music and what constitutes idiomatic writing for a vast array of lesser-known percussion instruments. Enrolment is open to graduate and upper-year undergraduate composers and to graduate and upper-year undergraduate percussionists who have some composing experience.
CMU420H1.prereqText: TMU231H1, Percussion and/or Composition majors or minors, P.I.

DMU313H1.name: Introduction to Music Recording
DMU313H1.title: Introduction to Music Recording
DMU313H1.description: Recording music has become an essential part of a musician’s career. With technological advancements and the ability to reach people worldwide, music has never been more accessible. Through lectures and hands-on tutorials, this course will introduce the student to the basic theory and practical skills required to record music.

HMU330H1.name: Musical Cultures: Latin America & the Caribbean
HMU330H1.title: Musical Cultures: Latin America & the Caribbean
HMU330H1.description: A survey of popular, folk, and religious traditions from English, French, Spanish, and Portuguese speaking countries in South and Central America and the Caribbean. These practices will be considered with an emphasis on the lasting impact of European colonization and the Atlantic slave trade, both of which deeply inform musical life in these parts of the world.

HMU405H1.name: All Hail the Queens: Gender, Urbanity, and the Culture of Hip Hop
HMU405H1.title: All Hail the Queens: Gender, Urbanity, and the Culture of Hip Hop
HMU405H1.description: Rooted in the music and street culture of Black and Latin American urban youth amid the rise of the post-industrial crisis, Hip Hop culture has been a masculinist terrain since its inception. While women and female identifying persons have been among the culture’s creators, they have not always been adequately commemorated as part of Hip Hop’s grand narrative, nor have they been appropriately credited for their contributions and innovations. Working against tremendous odds to contest their ongoing marginalization and objectification, women in Hip Hop developed gender-specific strategies to carve out greater space, access, expression, and representation. Using a variety of archival texts and mediums, this course will explore Hip Hop’s origins and the politics of historical erasure; race, ethnicity and Blackness; gender, queerness, and intersectionality; misogyny, gendered violence, and exploitation; resistive practices, sounds and performances; negotiations with power, capitalism and industry; and the rise of Hip Hop Feminisms.

PMU261H1.name: Introduction to Piano Teaching Methods
PMU261H1.title: Introduction to Piano Teaching Methods
PMU261H1.description: An introduction to historical keyboard technique treatises, as well as beginning and intermediate level learning theories and teaching methods.

ARC100H1.name: Drawing and Representation I
ARC100H1.title: Drawing and Representation I
ARC100H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC100H1.description: An introduction to the theories and techniques of visual communication and representation in the design disciplines delivered through a series of lectures and thematic drawing projects. The course serves as a hands-on introduction to representational and geometrical techniques in architecture, landscape architecture, and urbanism.

ARC180H1.name: Computation and Design
ARC180H1.title: Computation and Design
ARC180H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC180H1.description: An introduction to computational thought and techniques through a series of exercises, readings, and lectures. Students will investigate the relationship between generative design, culture, and technology in design and art before and after the advent of the digital.

ARC200H1.name: Drawing and Representation II
ARC200H1.title: Drawing and Representation II
ARC200H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC200H1.description: A course on the theories and techniques of visual communication and representation in the design disciplines delivered through lectures and thematic drawing projects. The course serves as a hands-on introduction to the description of structures and environments as a means of both production and critique. Students are strongly advised NOT to enroll into both ARC200H1 and ARC201H1 in the same semester.

ARC251H1.name: Close Readings in Architecture
ARC251H1.title: Close Readings in Architecture
ARC251H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC251H1.description: Detailed examination of case studies in the history of architecture with close attention to the objects of study. The relationship between design, context, and theory will be explored through analyses of artifacts and texts.

ARC281H1.name: Structures, Building Systems, and Environments I
ARC281H1.title: Structures, Building Systems, and Environments I
ARC281H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC281H1.description: An introduction to structural and environmental design, the technologies of building and landscape systems, and the methods and frameworks through which the built environment is constructed. The calculation of quantitative criteria is taught through first-principles explorations.

ARC351H1.name: Global Modernisms
ARC351H1.title: Global Modernisms
ARC351H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC351H1.description: An examination of the question of architectural modernism across the globe from the beginnings of colonialism up to the present moment. Themes relating to claims of universal validity, the transfer of professional knowledge, and political, social, and spatial contestations are examined through case studies.

ARC353H1.name: Architecture and Media
ARC353H1.title: Architecture and Media
ARC353H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC353H1.description: An exploration of the historical relationship between design and media.

ARC355H1.name: History of Urbanism
ARC355H1.title: History of Urbanism
ARC355H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC355H1.description: A consideration of urbanism through an examination of physical, social, economic, and political factors that have shaped cities and regions from the early modern period up to the present.

ARC356H1.name: Design History of Landscape Architecture
ARC356H1.title: Design History of Landscape Architecture
ARC356H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC356H1.description: An opportunity to build a historical and theoretical vocabulary for the designed environment. This course will include case studies at multiple scales, focusing on North American examples from the relatively recent past.

ARC361Y1.name: Architecture Studio III
ARC361Y1.title: Architecture Studio III
ARC361Y1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC361Y1.description: This studio will focus on residential types and the domestic environment through an exploration of the relationship between building types, tectonics, and material assemblies in an urban context.

ARC363Y1.name: Landscape Architecture Studio III
ARC363Y1.title: Landscape Architecture Studio III
ARC363Y1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC363Y1.description: This studio will address urban form, context, and significance as factors in the creation of public space, with a focus on sites at block and neighbourhood scales.

ARC369Y1.name: Comprehensive Studio III
ARC369Y1.title: Comprehensive Studio III
ARC369Y1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC369Y1.description: This Studio will provide a variety of design problems across different, nested scales, encouraging a comprehensive, multidisciplinary approach. It is a team-oriented project-based course in which students will determine and develop a collaborative project within the built or natural environment.
ARC369Y1.exclusionText: Available only to students enrolled in AHSPE1000 (Specialist in Architectural Studies: Comprehensive Stream), AHMAJ1000 (Major in Architectural Studies), or AHSPE1002 (Specialist in Architectural Studies: History and Theory of Architecture, Landscape, and Urbanism Stream)

ARC381Y1.name: Technology Studio IV
ARC381Y1.title: Technology Studio IV
ARC381Y1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC381Y1.description: This studio continues to explore the role of technology in design and promotes innovation in design tool development, building systems, simulation and visualization. Emphasis will be on applying knowledge gained in earlier coursework in a project-based studio setting using computational techniques, physical model making, and 1:1 fabrication and prototyping.

ARC382H1.name: Structures, Building Systems, and Environments II
ARC382H1.title: Structures, Building Systems, and Environments II
ARC382H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC382H1.description: Continued exploration of the principles of structural and environmental design, the technologies of building and landscape systems, and the methods and frameworks in which the built environment is constructed. The calculation of quantitative criteria is taught through first-principles explorations.

ARC386H1.name: Landscape Ecology
ARC386H1.title: Landscape Ecology
ARC386H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC386H1.description: An introduction to the principles of landscape ecology, addressing the application of evolving scientific understanding to contemporary landscape architecture and urban design practice.

ARC401H1.name: Senior Seminar (Research)
ARC401H1.title: Senior Seminar (Research)
ARC401H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC401H1.description: In this course, students will engage in research in response to issues of pressing disciplinary, societal, and personal concern within the built and natural environments.
ARC401H1.prereqText: 2.0 credits in ARC courses at the 300-level with a final grade of 80% or above and permission of the Program Director

ARC465H1.name: Advanced Topics in Architecture
ARC465H1.title: Advanced Topics in Architecture
ARC465H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC465H1.description: Examination of an advanced topic in the design of architecture. The focus of the course changes depending upon the instructors research specialty or current issues in architecture.
ARC465H1.prereqText: 1.0 credit at the 300-level in ARC courses

ARC466H1.name: Advanced Topics in Landscape Architecture
ARC466H1.title: Advanced Topics in Landscape Architecture
ARC466H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC466H1.description: Examination of an advanced topic in the design of landscape architecture. The focus of the course changes depending upon the instructors research specialty or current issues in landscape architecture.
ARC466H1.prereqText: 1.0 credit at the 300-level in ARC courses

ARC480H1.name: Advanced Topics in the Technology of Architecture
ARC480H1.title: Advanced Topics in the Technology of Architecture
ARC480H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC480H1.description: Examination of an advanced topic in the technology of architecture. The focus of the course changes depending upon the instructors research specialty or current issues in landscape architecture.
ARC480H1.prereqText: 1.0 credit at the 300-level in ARC courses.

JAV120H1.name: Visual Concepts
JAV120H1.title: Visual Concepts
JAV120H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
JAV120H1.description: An introduction to a wide range of topics situated in modernism, postmodernism, and the contemporary that inform current art practice and critical discourse. The course investigates post-1970 art practice through diverse societal, cultural, and political influences of contemporary critical thought.

JAV130H1.name: Visual Strategies
JAV130H1.title: Visual Strategies
JAV130H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
JAV130H1.description: An introduction to diverse mediums and topics for exploration with an emphasis on experimentation and conceptual development. In addition to acquiring manual skills used in production of contemporary visual art, students are encouraged to explore their own individual artistic and research processes.
JAV130H1.prereqText: JAV120H1/VIS120H1, or registration in the Bachelor of Arts Degree in Visual Studies

JAV151H1.name: History of Architecture, Landscape, Urbanism, and Art I
JAV151H1.title: History of Architecture, Landscape, Urbanism, and Art I
JAV151H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
JAV151H1.description: An introduction to the pre-industrial world through examples of architecture, landscape, sites, and art drawn from across the globe. The goal of this course is not only to explain the artifacts and sites under discussion but also to explain the social, economic, and cultural conditions of the world through them.

JAV200H1.name: Introduction to Critical Theory
JAV200H1.title: Introduction to Critical Theory
JAV200H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
JAV200H1.description: A course that teaches critical and analytical ways of engaging visual culture within an interdisciplinary and international setting. Students are introduced to foundational intellectual tools and a research methodology appropriate to artists, designers, and architects.

JAV303H1.name: Land, Relations, Truth and Reconciliation
JAV303H1.title: Land,  Relations, Truth and Reconciliation
JAV303H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
JAV303H1.description: The course considers interdisciplinary perspectives on sustainability within the built and natural environment. Through the examination of a broad set of textual and visual artifacts, students will critically examine responses to topics such as climate change, systemic inequity, and spatial justice at an individual, civic, regional, and planetary scale.

VIS201H1.name: Painting: Methods & Materials
VIS201H1.title: Painting: Methods and Materials
VIS201H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS201H1.description: This is a hands-on course that deals with technical and theoretical issues of contemporary painting. The act of painting and the relevance of painting are stressed through both historical and current issues.

VIS202H1.name: Artists' Moving Image I
VIS202H1.title: Artists' Moving Image I
VIS202H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS202H1.description: This course introduces students to the production of digital moving image artworks. Students are encouraged to work in all production and postproduction forms including live video recording, GIFs and animation. In addition to hands-on instruction to cameras and editing software, this course includes individual and group critiques, seminars, and critical viewing of contemporary moving image artworks.

VIS203H1.name: Time-Based Installation I
VIS203H1.title: Time-Based Installation I
VIS203H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS203H1.description: This studio course introduces students to creative coding practices and their use in the production of time-based installation art. Various site- and time-based art forms, including: audio installation, video installation, interactive installation, virtual environments, and digitally-based performance are considered through the introduction of emergent artistic technologies. Readings, gallery visits, screenings, and presentations provide context for these art practices. Responding to assignments and writing prompts, students produce projects that explore the complex interplay between digital media, time, and space.

VIS204H1.name: Installation Art I: Material and Sculptural Practices
VIS204H1.title: Installation Art I: Material and Sculptural Practices
VIS204H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS204H1.description: This course introduces students to the basic principles of working with materials to produce three-dimensional and installation-based artworks. This hands-on project-based course includes individual and group critiques, seminars with relevant readings and critical viewing of contemporary installation artworks.

VIS205H1.name: Drawing: Experimental Practices I
VIS205H1.title: Drawing: Experimental Practices I
VIS205H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS205H1.description: Studio-based projects explore contemporary drawing practice. Materials and approaches take into account historical practices while responding to changing cultural issues.

VIS212H1.name: Colour
VIS212H1.title: Colour
VIS212H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS212H1.description: An introductory course on colour that looks at its mechanics and interdisciplinary scope: from the history of science and culture to the technicalities of various colour spaces in both analog and digital environments. A combination of lectures, readings, and studio projects shape a broad understanding of both how colour has been used and how to use colour.

VIS217H1.name: Photobased (Chemical)
VIS217H1.title: Photo-based (Chemical)
VIS217H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS217H1.description: Photo-based projects in which the fundamentals of optical-chemical mechanical photographic processes and technologies are integrated with concepts in contemporary photo-based practice. Student must have 35mm camera that allows full manual control.

VIS218H1.name: Photobased (Digital)
VIS218H1.title: Photo-based (Digital)
VIS218H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS218H1.description: Photo-based projects in which the fundamentals of optical-digital photographic processes and technologies are integrated with concepts in contemporary photo-based practice.

VIS240H1.name: Sound Art I
VIS240H1.title: Sound Art I
VIS240H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS240H1.description: Introduction to sound art through studio projects such as field recording, sound walks, and multi-channel sound installation. Focus on listening and history of the genre explored through presentations, field trips and readings.

VIS302H1.name: Artists' Moving Image II
VIS302H1.title: Artists' Moving Image II
VIS302H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS302H1.description: Students continue to develop their skills in pre-production, production and post-production of digital media used in moving image artworks. Emphasis is placed on the conceptual development of projects, with class discussions and individual meetings focusing on all stages of works-in-progress. Strategies for distribution, exhibition and funding are examined.

VIS305H1.name: Drawing: Experimental Practices II
VIS305H1.title: Drawing: Experimental  Practices II
VIS305H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS305H1.description: This course continues to build on VIS205H1 Drawing: Experimental Practices. Experimenting with a wide-ranging set of concepts, materials, techniques, and processes, students further explore the potential of drawing beyond its traditional and preconceived limits.

VIS310H1.name: Imaging the Political
VIS310H1.title: Imaging the Political
VIS310H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS310H1.description: Studio projects complemented by seminars and readings examine plastic, social, and gender politics in contemporary visual art.
VIS310H1.prereqText: 0.5 credit at the 200 or higher-level in VIS courses, JAV200H1/VIS200H1

VIS312H1.name: Collage
VIS312H1.title: Collage
VIS312H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS312H1.description: An investigation of historical and contemporary art incorporating collage as a central methodology. The evolution of collage as a means of expression is explored through studio-based projects and lectures.
VIS312H1.prereqText: 0.5 credit at the 200 or higher-level in VIS courses, JAV200H1/VIS200H1

VIS313H1.name: The Body
VIS313H1.title: The Body
VIS313H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS313H1.description: This studio-based, open-media course challenges conventional ideas about the body by examining developments in technology, culture, and politics. Through projects, lectures and readings, this course considers the fluidity of concepts such as gender, beauty, and ability as interpreted through representations of the body.
VIS313H1.prereqText: 0.5 credit at the 200 or higher-level in VIS courses.

VIS319H1.name: Defining Landscapes
VIS319H1.title: Defining Landscapes
VIS319H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS319H1.description: The concept of landscape is an entry point for investigating the relationship between people and their environments. Through exploration in open media studio projects, written work, readings, and seminars, this course provides an opportunity to critically examine historic and contemporary artist practices around the complex and difficult positioning of landscape as a source of inspiration and as a vehicle of expression while questioning these definitions in relation to capitalism, empire, and colonialism.
VIS319H1.prereqText: 0.5 credit at the 200 or higher-level in VIS courses.

VIS323H1.name: Painting: Contemporary Practice
VIS323H1.title: Painting: Contemporary Practice
VIS323H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS323H1.description: Painting: Contemporary Practice introduces philosophical and theoretical issues raised by the conceptual relationship of painting to other artistic strategies and the contemporary environment. Studio work will be complemented by the study of advanced artists working in this medium.

VIS326H1.name: Studio Practice
VIS326H1.title: Studio Practice
VIS326H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS326H1.description: A project-based studio course in which each student works to advance and to articulate their visual arts practice, and to develop individual process, themes and influences, the articulation. Group critiques, seminars, reading and writing assignments. Open media, students must have access to own means of production.
VIS326H1.prereqText: 1.0 credit at the 200 or higher-level in VIS courses.

VIS330H1.name: Artists' Writings
VIS330H1.title: Artists' Writings
VIS330H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS330H1.description: A survey course of writings that artists have produced across history exploring all forms: manifestos, plays, novels, short stories, art reviews, theoretical, art historical, artist statements, and interventions. Artists writings are explored as a genre as well as gestures through which artists have entered a professional discourse. Students will explore various genres of writing in the course.

VIS331H1.name: Art Criticism
VIS331H1.title: Art Criticism
VIS331H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS331H1.description: Criticism is a practice of writing distinct from academic argumentation or artists' writings, with a long history in periodicals, newspapers, and exhibition catalogues. The course surveys the genre to analyze key texts that have shaped the narrative of art leading to, and including, the current discourse. Students both read and write criticism in the course, experimenting with voice, rhetoric, and polemics.

VIS421H1.name: Institutions and Exhibitions
VIS421H1.title: Institutions and Exhibitions
VIS421H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS421H1.description: A course in which students engage a variety of exhibition types in their institutional context: government museums, artist-run centres (ARC), cultural non-profits, media distribution centres, tourist museums, commercial galleries, private museums, collectives, pop-ups, community centres, etc. Students conduct site visits and analyze the architecture, economic models, audience, and content of various institutions.
VIS421H1.prereqText: 0.5 credit at the 200 or higher-level in VIS courses, JAV200H1/VIS200H1

ARC451H1.name: Advanced Topics in the History and Theory of Architecture
ARC451H1.title: Advanced Topics in the History and Theory of Architecture
ARC451H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC451H1.description: Examination of an advanced topic in the history and theory of architecture. The focus of the course changes depending on the instructors research specialty as well as current issues.
ARC451H1.prereqText: 1.0 credit at the 300-level in ARC courses

VIS405H1.name: Visual Studies Internship
VIS405H1.title: Visual Studies Internship
VIS405H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS405H1.description: A one semester Internship provides placement at a gallery, media-arts centre, artist-run centre, artist, or publication with a focus on contemporary art practice
VIS405H1.prereqText: 1.0 credit at the 200 or higher-level in VIS courses, JAV200H1/VIS200H1, 1.0 credit at the 300-level in VIS courses, and permission of Program Director.

VIS404H1.name: Independent Studies
VIS404H1.title: Independent Studies
VIS404H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS404H1.description: Individual advanced projects undertaken under the supervision of Visual Studies Faculty. Student meets regularly with faculty supervisor who provides individual critiques of research and artworks produced. The course culminates in an exhibition of the artwork(s) produced over the course of the term.
VIS404H1.prereqText: 1.0 credit at the 200 or higher-level in VIS courses, JAV200H1/VIS200H1, 1.0 credit at the 300-level in VIS courses, and permission of Program Director.

ARC397H1.name: Independent Study
ARC397H1.title: Independent Study
ARC397H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC397H1.description: An independent research project to be proposed by the student and supervised by a full-time faculty member affiliated with the Daniels Faculty. Students wishing to take this course must have the permission of the Architectural Studies Program Director and of the prospective supervisor.
ARC397H1.prereqText: 1.0 credit at the 300-level in ARC courses. An application must be submitted to the Program Director.

ARC112H1.name: Design + Engineering I
ARC112H1.title: Design & Engineering I
ARC112H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC112H1.description: A studio-based introduction to the methods and processes of design. The course serves as a hands-on exploration of design issues through a series of exercises that introduce students to the conceptual underpinnings of the design process, developing their capacity to conceive, manipulate, and analyze form through a variety of representational media. In collaboration with the foundational course in first-year engineering, students will conduct client-driven community-based research in response to design problems.

ARC181H1.name: Technologies of Architecture, Landscape, Urbanism, and Art I
ARC181H1.title: Technologies of Architecture, Landscape, Urbanism, and Art I
ARC181H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC181H1.description: An introduction to how technology has shaped the disciplines of design and art through a series of case studies that describe paradigmatic episodes at the nexus of architecture, landscape architecture, urbanism, and art.

ARC201H1.name: Design Studio II: How to design almost nothing
ARC201H1.title: Design Studio II
ARC201H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC201H1.description: A studio-based introduction to design with emphasis upon the production of form and space and the formation of landscapes. The course serves as a hands-on exploration of the relationships between material, tectonic, and programmatic organizations in the context of social, technological, and environmental concerns. Students are strongly advised NOT to enroll into both ARC200H1 and ARC201H1 in the same semester.

ARC252H1.name: Close Readings in Landscape Architecture
ARC252H1.title: Close Readings in Landscape Architecture
ARC252H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC252H1.description: Detailed examination of case studies in the history of landscape architecture with close attention to the objects of study. The relationship between design, context, and theory will be explored through analyses of artifacts and texts.

ARC253H1.name: Close Readings in Urban Design
ARC253H1.title: Close Readings in Urban Design
ARC253H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC253H1.description: Detailed examination of case studies in the history of urbanism with close attention to the objects of study. The relationship between design, context, and theory will be explored through analyses of artifacts and texts.

ARC280H1.name: Modeling and Fabrication in Design
ARC280H1.title: Modeling and Fabrication in Design
ARC280H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC280H1.description: An introduction to the theories and technologies of modeling. The emphasis of the course will be on the exploration of the relationship between technology and design conceptualization with the aim of developing skills to construct techniques for effective visual communication. The course will be delivered through a series of lectures and workshops.

ARC302H1.name: Exploring Design Practices
ARC302H1.title: Exploring Design Practices
ARC302H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC302H1.description: An introduction to the practice of architecture, landscape architecture, urbanism, and visual art through a series of case studies and guest lectures. These classes will be integrated with the lecture series to provide opportunities for students to engage with leading practitioners in design and art.

ARC352H1.name: History of Architectural Knowledge
ARC352H1.title: History of Architectural Knowledge
ARC352H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC352H1.description: An exploration of the ways in which architecture has made claims to knowledge through various means textual and non-textual since the early modern period.

ARC354H1.name: History of Housing
ARC354H1.title: History of Housing
ARC354H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC354H1.description: An exploration of the question of housing since the beginning of the Industrial Revolution.

ARC357H1.name: Environmental History of Landscape Architecture
ARC357H1.title: Environmental History of Landscape Architecture
ARC357H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC357H1.description: An examination of the global history of the interrelations between societies and their environment. This course examines the organization of landscape and urban systems in a variety of geographic and cultural regions across the globe and over large spans of time. Please note that ARC356H1 Design History of Landscape Architecture is recommended as background for this course.
ARC357H1.prereqText: ARC251H1/ARC252H1/ARC253H1/1.0 FCE in ARC 200+ level lecture courses

ARC362Y1.name: Architecture Studio IV
ARC362Y1.title: Architecture Studio IV
ARC362Y1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC362Y1.description: This studio will focus on the design of a public program or institution in an urban setting through an exploration of the relationship between building types, tectonics, and material assemblies in an urban context.

ARC364Y1.name: Landscape Architecture Studio IV
ARC364Y1.title: Landscape Architecture Studio IV
ARC364Y1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC364Y1.description: This studio will examine the reciprocal influences of landscape and urbanism, with respect to form and process, through a focus on landscapes as urban systems at multiple scales.

ARC365H1.name: Selected Topics in Architecture
ARC365H1.title: Selected Topics in Architecture
ARC365H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC365H1.description: Examination of a selected topic in the design of architecture. The focus of the course changes depending upon the instructors research specialty or current issues in architecture.

ARC366H1.name: Selected Topics in Landscape Architecture
ARC366H1.title: Selected Topics in Landscape Architecture
ARC366H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC366H1.description: Examination of a selected topic in the design of landscape architecture. The focus of the course changes depending upon the instructors research specialty or current issues in landscape architecture.

ARC367H1.name: Selected Topics in Urban Design
ARC367H1.title: Selected Topics in Urban Design
ARC367H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC367H1.description: Examination of a selected topic in the design of urbanism. The focus of the course changes depending upon the instructors research specialty or current issues in urban design.

ARC380Y1.name: Technology Studio III
ARC380Y1.title: Technology Studio III
ARC380Y1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC380Y1.description: This studio applies knowledge obtained from the prerequisite courses towards project-based design work with the aim of facilitating an understanding of the relationship between emerging digital technologies and production in architecture, landscape architecture, and urbanism through the development of computational tools and algorithmic design.

ARC383H1.name: Technologies of Architecture, Landscape, Urbanism, and Art II
ARC383H1.title: Technologies of Architecture, Landscape, Urbanism, and Art II
ARC383H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC383H1.description: Building upon the themes and topics explored in Technologies of Architecture, Landscape, Urbanism, and Art I, this course will investigate how technology has shaped the disciplines of design and art through a series of case studies that describe paradigmatic episodes at the nexus of architecture, landscape architecture, urbanism, and art.
ARC383H1.prereqText: ARC181H1 and 1.0 credit in ARC200-level lecture courses

ARC385H1.name: Physical Computing
ARC385H1.title: Physical Computing
ARC385H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC385H1.description: An exploration of the relationship between computation design and approaches to physical interaction. The course will explore a range of approaches for integrating computation into the physical realm through a series of projects using physical computing prototyping tools.

ARC387H1.name: Landscape Topography and Hydrology
ARC387H1.title: Landscape Topography and Hydrology
ARC387H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC387H1.description: An introduction to the manipulation of landform and water in the urban context, studied through digital fabrication and metrics.

ARC402Y1.name: Senior Seminar (Thesis)
ARC402Y1.title: Senior Seminar (Thesis)
ARC402Y1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC402Y1.description: In this course, students develop and complete a thesis project in response to issues of pressing disciplinary, societal, and personal concern within the built and natural environments.
ARC402Y1.prereqText: ARC401H1 with a final grade of 80% and permission of the Program Director

ARC467H1.name: Advanced Topics in Urban Design
ARC467H1.title: Advanced Topics in Urban Design
ARC467H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC467H1.description: Examination of an advanced topic in the design of urbanism. The focus of the course changes depending upon the instructors research specialty or current issues in urban design.
ARC467H1.prereqText: 1.0 credit at the 300-level in ARC courses

ARC491H1.name: Multidisciplinary Capstone Design Seminar
ARC491H1.title: Multidisciplinary Capstone Design Seminar
ARC491H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC491H1.description: The seminar is an optional co-requisite available to students participating in ARC490Y or ARC492Y. It offers a critical consideration of ongoing design work for their respective Capstone Projects in a series of collaborative sessions, and allows students to advance aspects of their multidisciplinary designs through an architectural, urban or landscape design lens. This includes the creation of portfolio or multimedia content as a final stage of the design process. The course will include group meetings, pinups and presentations, and independent design work.

JAV101H1.name: Design Studio I: How to design almost anything
JAV101H1.title: Design Studio I
JAV101H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
JAV101H1.description: A studio-based introduction to the methods and processes of design. The course serves as a hands-on exploration of design issues through a series of exercises that introduce students to the conceptual underpinnings of the design process, developing their capacity to conceive, manipulate, and analyze form through a variety of representational media.

JAV152H1.name: History of Architecture, Landscape, Urbanism, and Art II
JAV152H1.title: History of Architecture, Landscape, Urbanism, and Art II
JAV152H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
JAV152H1.description: An introduction to the post-industrial world through examples of architecture, landscape, sites, and art drawn from across the globe. The goal of this course is not only to explain the artifacts and sites under discussion but also to explain the social, economic, and cultural conditions of the world through them.

VIS209H1.name: Contemporary Printing
VIS209H1.title: Contemporary Printing
VIS209H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS209H1.description: Introduction to contemporary printmaking that covers publishing to 3D printing. This course looks at the concept of copying and producing one of a kind artifacts. Drawing on both centuries old techniques and the most modern technologies, students will explore what it means to make an image in the contemporary moment.

VIS211H1.name: Works on Paper
VIS211H1.title: Works on Paper
VIS211H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS211H1.description: A studio based course which explores the potential of paper from drawing to object making, in the context of contemporary art practice.

VIS220H1.name: Painting and the Subject
VIS220H1.title: Painting and the Subject
VIS220H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS220H1.description: Representation and abstraction are investigated through the development of themes drawn from personal, social and cultural sources.

VIS303H1.name: Time-Based Installation II
VIS303H1.title: Time-Based Installation II
VIS303H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS303H1.description: This project-based course advances students’ development in conceptualizing and producing time-based art installations, including studio experimentation and creation with audio, video, interactive performance, and other forms of time-based media used by contemporary artists, such as creative computation. Seminars, readings and writing prompts augment the self-directed projects produced by the students.

VIS306H1.name: Installation Art II: Contextual Practices
VIS306H1.title: Installation Art II: Contextual Practices
VIS306H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS306H1.description: An investigation into the history and practice of site/installation and three dimensional fabrication through slide lectures, projects and seminar discussions. Earth works, large scale public projects, and site specific installations will be explored.

VIS316H1.name: The Constructed Image
VIS316H1.title: The Constructed Image
VIS316H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS316H1.description: Through research, concept development, as well as direct engagement with materials and processes, students will explore the constructed image and constructedness as an intersection of theory and practice.
VIS316H1.prereqText: 0.5 credit at the 200 or higher-level in VIS courses.

VIS318H1.name: Integrated Photobased Explorations
VIS318H1.title: Integrated Photo-based Explorations
VIS318H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS318H1.description: Studio projects exploring contemporary photographic issues and practice; seminars and readings are integral.

VIS320H1.name: Critical Curatorial Lab
VIS320H1.title: Critical Curatorial Lab
VIS320H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS320H1.description: Projects and seminars develop an understanding of curatorial and critical practice in contemporary visual and media arts.
VIS320H1.prereqText: 0.5 credit at the 200 or higher-level in VIS courses.

VIS321H1.name: Artists' Multiples
VIS321H1.title: Artists' Multiples
VIS321H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS321H1.description: Production of artists multiples in various media is augmented with gallery and archive visits, screenings, and artist talks. Historical and contemporary technologies for reproduction are examined.
VIS321H1.prereqText: 0.5 credit at the 200 or higher-level in VIS courses.

VIS324H1.name: The Aesthetics of Everyday Life
VIS324H1.title: The Aesthetics of Everyday Life
VIS324H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS324H1.description: This interdisciplinary seminar course examines the aesthetic qualities of objects and experiences through the lens of scholarly research in its various methodologies, including historical and contemporary philosophy, critical theory, media theory, material practice, intergenerational dialogue, and lived experience.
VIS324H1.prereqText: 0.5 credit at the 200 or higher-level in VIS courses.

VIS328H1.name: Publishing Platforms
VIS328H1.title: Publishing Platforms
VIS328H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS328H1.description: From manifestos for avant-garde art and architecture movements to contemporary digital exchanges, publishing has played an important role in both the development of aesthetic discourse and as a primary platform for creation. This course combines both the seminar format for looking at the history of publishing as well as a studio environment for participants who will create publishing platforms such as posters, journals, serial magazines, artists books, pamphlets, micro-presses, blogs, websites, and social media.

VIS332H1.name: Advanced Critical Theory
VIS332H1.title: Advanced Critical Theory
VIS332H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS332H1.description: A continuation of philosophic and theoretical writings first introduced in JAV200. Concepts in epistemology, psychoanalysis, socio-political thought, economic theory, visual culture, semiotics, material culture, feminism, queer studies, postcolonial theory, critical race theory, and indigenous studies are explored through primary texts.

VIS340H1.name: Sound Art II
VIS340H1.title: Sound Art II
VIS340H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS340H1.description: Exploration and experimentation in advanced sound artworks. Building from projects first conducted in the intro prerequisite course, this course further considers architectural acoustics, politics of soundscapes, sonification and music in relation to contemporary art. Course content is composed of studio projects, presentations and seminars.

VIS406H1.name: Public Art
VIS406H1.title: Public Art
VIS406H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS406H1.description: This course is an introduction into the complex process of public art. Through lectures, projects, seminars and field trips the student will develop a clearer understanding of the collaborative nature of public production around key issues such as advocacy, environmental ethics, and the sensual nature of space.
VIS406H1.prereqText: 1.0 credit at the 200 or higher-level in VIS courses, JAV200H1/ VIS200H1, VIS306H1 or permission of Program Director.

VIS420H1.name: Advanced Readings in Contemporary Art and Culture
VIS420H1.title: Advanced Readings in Contemporary Art and Culture
VIS420H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS420H1.description: A seminar course that investigates current issues in contemporary art. Focus is on contemporary theoretical readings and classic texts. The focus of topic changes each offering pending instructors research specialty and current issues.
VIS420H1.prereqText: 0.5 credit at the 200 or higher-level in VIS courses, JAV200H1/VIS200H1

VIS426H1.name: Studio Practice II
VIS426H1.title: Studio Practice II
VIS426H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS426H1.description: This course allows students to pursue their own, independently-guided advanced projects. Students will establish their research interests and paths, and will work with their peers and the instructor to refine, test, and use their research towards a resolved final project. The work made for this course is not limited to any form or medium and will be solely determined by each student's interests. The course will consist of student-led seminars, discussions, and critiques with ample in-class time to work on projects and for one-on-one discussions with the instructor.
VIS426H1.prereqText: JAV200H1/VIS200H1, VIS326 or 1.0 credit at the 300 or higher level in VIS courses and permission of instructor

VIS307H1.name: Art and Context
VIS307H1.title: Art and Context
VIS307H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
VIS307H1.description: Applying art to the borders of other disciplines or issues within the university community, students develop projects with the objective of opening spaces for discourse: art as a transgressive device.
VIS307H1.prereqText: 0.5 credit at the 200 or higher-level in VIS courses, JAV200H1/VIS200H1

ARC426H1.name: Working with Wood
ARC426H1.title: Working with Wood
ARC426H1.division: Architecture, Landscape, and Design, John H. Daniels Faculty of
ARC426H1.description: Wood has been an important building material throughout the ages and in today's world has taken on the added importance of being a renewable and sustainable material that assists with greenhouse gas mitigation strategies. This course will provide students with an understanding of wood’s unique physical properties, the variability of these properties within different species and how these properties can inform its proper use in various applications. The Canadian forestry industry sets the context for this course acknowledging that forests transcend political borders and reach around the world.
ARC426H1.prereqText: 1.0 credit at the 300-level in ARC courses
